events.title: William III and Mary II Crowned
events.description: William III and Mary II were crowned joint sovereigns in a ceremony that also marked the Scottish Parliament's agreement with the English decision to offer them the throne.
events.significance: The coronation sealed the Glorious Revolution settlement. It strengthened Parliament's power over the monarchy and shaped British constitutional government.

events.title: Napoleon Abdicates and Is Exiled to Elba
events.description: After the Allies captured Paris, Napoleon Bonaparte gave up his throne as Emperor of France. He was exiled to the Mediterranean island of Elba.
events.significance: The abdication ended Napoleon's first reign and reshaped Europe. He escaped Elba less than a year later, which led to the Hundred Days and Waterloo.

events.title: Edo Castle Surrenders, Ending the Tokugawa Shogunate
events.description: Former shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu handed Edo Castle over to Imperial forces, which ended more than 250 years of Tokugawa rule.
events.significance: The surrender cleared the way for the Meiji Restoration. Japan then modernized rapidly and emerged as a major world power.

events.title: Titanic Leaves Queenstown on Its Final Stop
events.description: The RMS Titanic left Queenstown, Ireland, and set out across the Atlantic for New York City. It was the liner's last port of call before it sank.
events.significance: The departure began the last leg of the Titanic's only voyage. The sinking became one of history's best-known maritime disasters and led to major reforms in ship safety.

events.title: Buchenwald Concentration Camp Is Liberated
events.description: Allied forces liberated Buchenwald, one of the largest Nazi concentration camps on German soil. Prisoners had also taken action inside the camp as American troops approached.
events.significance: The liberation exposed Nazi atrocities to the world. It remains a key part of Holocaust remembrance.
